label: Rabbits arrive
detail: A Victorian grazier releases rabbits for sport hunting.

label: Fences go up
detail: Western Australia builds three rabbit-proof fences between 1902 and 1907 to stop rabbits spreading west.

label: 70% of the continent
detail: Within about 70 years rabbits cover 70% of Australia, the fastest known invasion by a mammal anywhere.

label: 600 million rabbits
detail: Numbers peak at an estimated 600 million. Myxomatosis is released, the world's first virus used against a pest mammal.

label: Rabbits fight back
detail: By the late 1950s rabbits and virus have adapted to each other and the disease is less deadly.

label: Calicivirus
detail: With numbers back at about 300 million, rabbit haemorrhagic disease virus (RHDV) gets out during field trials; it is officially released in 1996.

label: RHDV2 arrives
detail: A new strain is found and crosses the continent within 18 months, cutting wild rabbit numbers by about 60%.

label: K5 released
detail: The first nationally coordinated release of a new calicivirus strain in 20 years.
